subject: Maths
topic: Four Operations and Order of Operations
title: Multi-step calculations
subtitle: Four Operations and Order of Operations · KS3 Maths
learning_objective: I can solve problems that require more than one step, choosing the correct operations.

key_vocab.definition: A multi-step calculation requires you to perform two or more operations in sequence to reach the answer.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can solve problems that require more than one step, choosing the correct operations.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: multi-step calculation -- A multi-step calculation requires you to perform two or more operations in sequence to reach the answer.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Break the problem into steps. Solve each step in order. Check your answer makes sense.
Step 1 → Step 2 → Answer
One step at a time

Key examples:
  ✓ Read → Plan → Calculate → Check  (4 steps)
  ✓ Break complex problems into parts  (simplify)
  ✓ Use BIDMAS for order of operations  (always)
  ✗ Just do operations left to right  (must use BIDMAS)
  ✗ Only use one operation per problem  (multi-step needs more)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – shopping problem
  Buy 3 shirts at £12 each and 2 pairs of socks at £3.50. Total cost?
  Shirts: 3 × 12 = £36
  Socks: 2 × 3.50 = £7
  Total: 36 + 7 = £43
  = £43
  (Calculate each item separately, then add.)

Example 2 – with change
  You pay for a £7.80 item with a £20 note. How many 50p coins in your change?
  Change: 20 − 7.80 = £12.20
  Divide by 0.50: 12.20 ÷ 0.50 = 24.4
  = 24 complete 50p coins (with 20p left)
  = 24 coins
  (Find the change first, then divide by the coin value.)

sections.title: Money problems
sections.content:
Show your working.

(a) 5 items at £4.50. Change from £30?
(b) 3 meals at £8.95 + 2 drinks at £2.30. Total?
(c) Earn £9.50/hour for 8 hours. Spend £45. Left?
(d) Buy 4 at £6.25. Pay with 2 × £20 notes. Change?

sections.title: Rate problems
sections.content:
Calculate step by step.

(a) 60 mph for 3 hours then 45 mph for 2 hours. Total miles?
(b) Type 50 words/min for 12 min. How many words?
(c) Fill 8 litres/min for 5 min, drain 3 litres/min for 4 min. Net?
(d) Earn £12/hr weekday, £18/hr weekend. Work 30 + 8 hrs. Total?

sections.title: Real-life multi-step
sections.content:
Read carefully and solve.

(a) Bus fare £2.40 each way, 5 days/week. Weekly cost?
(b) Recipe for 4: needs 300g flour. How much for 10 people?
(c) Pool: 25m. Swim 12 lengths. Total in km?
(d) 6 eggs/box, need 50 eggs. How many boxes to buy?

sections.title: Mixed multi-step
sections.content:
Solve each problem. Show steps.

(a) Buy 3 at £7.99, get 10% off total. Pay?
(b) Score 72, 85, 64. Need average of 75. What fourth score needed?
(c) Area of room 5m × 4m. Tiles are 0.5m × 0.5m. How many tiles?
(d) Train at 120 km/h for 45 min. Distance in km?
(e) 12 sweets shared so ratio 1:2:3. Middle pile?

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ Multi-step problems need more than one operation
✗ Always add all the numbers in a word problem
✓ Break problems into smaller steps
✗ The operations are always stated explicitly
✓ Check your answer makes sense in context
